scope.flow: FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds() unrestricted rebalancing with external custodian transfer
scope.environment: FastAccessVault contract with custodian address possibly a contract; ERC777 or callback-enabled tokens possible
evidence: FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds() Lacks Access Control and Reentrancy Protection, Enabling Griefing and DoS Attacks

The `FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds()` function has no access control modifier, allowing anyone to trigger vault rebalancing at will. Combined with the external call to the custodian address (which could be a contract), this creates multiple attack vectors:
- Line 176: `_vaultToken.transfer(custodian, excess)` is external call
- No `nonReentrant` modifier on `rebalanceFunds()`
- Malicious custodian contract can re-enter during transfer
- With ERC777 tokens or callback-enabled tokens, can drain excess twice

ambiguities: Reentrancy and double-drain are conditional on custodian being a malicious contract and callback-enabled tokens; not asserted as observed.
Race-condition under-collateralization requires a prior redemption via processTransfer() reducing vault balance; report does not establish such a prior transaction.
Report does not specify whether rebalanceFunds() has any other guard (e.g., state checks) beyond lacking access control and nonReentrant.
Additional claimed effects (gas costs, reputation damage, operational overhead) are not included as separate impacts.
